mainTopic: Whether a כהן may become טמא for his father when the body is not whole: the beheaded father, מת מצוה, and ברייתות about limbs, bones and partial skeletons
overview: רב חסדא quotes רב: if a כהן's father's head was cut off, the son may not become טמא for him, because the פסוק says 'לאביו', meaning only when the father is whole. רב המנונא challenges this with a father beheaded by robbers on the road. רב חסדא answers that such a father is a מת מצוה, and a כהן must become טמא for any מת מצוה, so surely he must for his own father. The גמרא asks how he can be a מת מצוה when his son is there, and answers that someone on the road counts as having no one to bury him. Next the גמרא brings a ברייתא that lets a כהן search for a barley-sized bone, which seems to show he becomes טמא even when the body is missing a little. The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who allows טומאה even for a limb of a dead father. Finally, a ברייתא of רב כהנא בר' אליעזר בן יעקב allows a כהן to become טמא for a spine, a skull, or most of the skeleton, which challenges רב again. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A כהן does not become impure for a father whose head was cut off
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes רב: a כהן may not become טמא for his father if the father's head was cut off. The reason is that the פסוק 'לאביו' applies only when the father is whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רב: if a man's father's head was cut off, the son (a כהן) may not become impure to bury him. Why? The פסוק says 'for his father', meaning when the father is whole, not when he is missing a part.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב: a כהן may become טמא for his father only when the father's body is whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן normally may not become טמא for a dead body, except for close relatives like his father. רב reads the word 'לאביו' as describing the father in his complete form. So if the body is missing its head, the permission for the son does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: becomes ritually impure (here: by tending to a dead body)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the subject of the whole section. Every challenge that follows is testing whether it holds up.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Rav said:
If the head of his father was cut off,
he does not become impure for him.
phrases.notes: 'He' means the son, who is a כהן.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The verse says: 'for his father',
when he is whole,
and not when he is lacking.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן does not become טמא for his father whose head was severed, because 'לאביו' means only when the father is whole.

steps.title: What about a father beheaded by robbers on the road?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא challenges רב: if robbers cut off a traveler's head, would his son the כהן really not bury him?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said to him: But if so, take a man walking in the valley of ערבות whose head was cut off by robbers. Would you also say his son should not become impure to bury him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא attacks רב's rule with a case where it seems impossible to leave the father unburied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule is simply 'not whole means no permission', then a father beheaded by robbers would be left alone by his own son. That seems unacceptable, so the rule looks too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (introduces a result that seems wrong)

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said to him:
But if so,
if he was walking in the valley of Aravot,
and robbers cut off his head,
would you also say that he should not become impure for him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a כהן does not become טמא for a father who is not whole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Applying the rule to a father beheaded by robbers leads to the unacceptable result that his own son would not bury him.

steps.title: A father killed on the road is a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the robbers' case is a מת מצוה. A כהן must become טמא even for a stranger who is a מת מצוה, so surely he must for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are you talking about a מת מצוה? If a כהן is obligated to become impure for others in that situation, then for his own father, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends רב's rule by saying the robbers' case falls under a different rule, מת מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule only removes the special permission a son has for his father. It does not cancel the separate duty to bury a מת מצוה, which applies even to a stranger. This is a כל שכן: if he must do it for anyone, surely he must for his father.

keyTerms.meaning: a dead person with no one else to bury him; everyone, even a כהן, must bury him
now (introduces a 'how much more so' argument)

phrases.english: He said to him:
Are you speaking of a corpse with no one to bury it?
Now, one can say:
for others he is obligated,
for his father, is it not all the more so?

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifies the case under a different rule (מת מצוה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The robbers' case would leave the father unburied under רב's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The robbers' case is a מת מצוה, so the son must become טמא anyway; רב's rule applies only where the father is not a מת מצוה.

steps.title: How can it be a מת מצוה if he has a son?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether the father is really a מת מצוה. A ברייתא says someone who has people to bury him is not a מת מצוה, and here the father has a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this a מת מצוה? A ברייתא teaches: Who is a מת מצוה? Anyone who has no one to bury him. If one could call out and others would answer, he is not a מת מצוה. And here the father has a son!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's answer by quoting the definition of מת מצוה from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מת מצוה is only someone with nobody to bury him. The father's son is right there, so the father seems to have someone. If so, he is not a מת מצוה, and רב חסדא's answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא?
he calls out and others answer

phrases.english: But is this a met מצוה?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:
Which is a met מצוה?
Anyone who has no one to bury him.
If he calls and others answer him,
this is not a met מצוה.
And this one has a son!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that the beheaded traveler is a מת מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the ברייתא's definition, someone who has a person to bury him is not a מת מצוה, and this father has his son.

steps.title: A traveler on the road counts as having no one to bury him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that since the father was traveling on the road, he is treated like someone with no one to bury him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he was traveling on the road, he is considered like someone who has no one to bury him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and keeps רב חסדא's answer standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Out on the road, far from a community, there are no people to call for help with the burial. So even with his son there, the father still has the status of a מת מצוה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule (no טומאה for a father who is not whole) does not cancel the duty to bury a מת מצוה. A father killed on the road counts as a מת מצוה, so his son the כהן must bury him.

phrases.english: Since he was traveling on the road,
he is considered like one who has no one to bury him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the definition of מת מצוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Having a son present means the father is not a מת מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Someone who dies on the road counts as having no one to bury him, even if his son is there.

steps.title: A ברייתא about limbs and bones seems to challenge רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: the פסוק 'לה יטמא' teaches that a כהן does not become טמא for his relative's limbs, because he does not become טמא for a limb cut from his living father. Yet he may search for a bone the size of a barley grain. This seems to go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection was raised: 'For her he shall become impure' teaches that he becomes impure for her, but not for her limbs. This is because he does not become impure for a limb cut off from his living father. But he may search for a bone the size of a barley grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב's rule. Step 7 explains exactly where the contradiction lies, and step 8 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from 'לה' that a כהן does not become טמא for a limb cut from a living relative. Its last line, that he may search for a barley-sized bone, is the part the גמרא will use against רב. Step 7 spells out why.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from an earlier source)
a limb cut off from a living person
a bone the size of a barley grain

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge to רב does not come from the rule about limbs. It comes from the last line, about searching for a barley-sized bone, as the next step explains.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'For her he shall become impure',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:3, about the כהן's unmarried sister.

phrases.english: for her he becomes impure,
but he does not become impure for her limbs.
Because he does not become impure
for a limb from his living father.
But he may search
for a bone the size of a barley grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב's original rule from step 1 and challenges it from a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a כהן does not become טמא for a father who is not whole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets the כהן search for a barley-sized bone. As step 7 explains, this implies he becomes טמא for his father even when the body is missing a little.

steps.title: Why the barley-sized bone seems to go against רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem: if the כהן searches for even a tiny missing bone, that suggests he becomes טמא even when his father's body is missing a little.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it mean that 'he searches for a bone the size of a barley grain'? Doesn't it mean that even if the father's body is missing a small piece, the son still becomes טמא for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining exactly how the ברייתא from the last step goes against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said a כהן becomes טמא for his father only if the body is whole. The ברייתא says the כהן may search for a tiny bone. That suggests he deals with the body even when a small piece is missing, which looks like a contradiction to רב.

keyTerms.meaning: a bone the size of a barley grain

phrases.english: What is meant by "he searches
for a bone the size of a barley grain"?
Is it not to say
that even if he is missing a little, [the son becomes טמא for him]?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״מְחַזֵּיר הוּא עַל עֶצֶם כִּשְׂעוֹרָה״? לָאו לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the challenge that step 6 raised against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a כהן becomes טמא for his father only when the body is whole.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the כהן searches for even a tiny missing bone, he must become טמא even when the body is not complete.

steps.title: That ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the barley-bone ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. He holds a כהן becomes טמא even for a limb of his dead father, and רב simply does not follow that view.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. That ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: 'For her he becomes טמא, but not for her limbs.' This means he does not become טמא for a limb cut off his father while the father was alive. But he does become טמא for a limb from his father after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and רב does not have to agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the פסוק 'לה יטמא' only leaves out a limb cut from a living person. So for a dead father, even a single limb is enough, and that is why searching for a small bone makes sense in his view. רב follows the other view, which requires the whole body.

keyTerms.meaning: a limb cut from a living person
a limb from a dead body

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה reads 'not for her limbs' as only leaving out limbs cut from a living person. A limb from a dead father is still allowed in his view.

phrases.english: No, that [ברייתא] is רבי יהודה.
As it was taught: רבי יהודה says:
For her he becomes טמא,
but he does not become טמא for her limbs.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִיטַּמֵּא עַל אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי שֶׁל אָבִיו,
phrases.english: For he does not become טמא for a limb cut from his living father,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִיטַּמֵּא הוּא לְאֵבֶר מִן הַמֵּת שֶׁל אָבִיו.
phrases.english: but he does become טמא for a limb from his dead father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by assigning that ברייתא to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא whom רב does not follow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barley-bone ברייתא is a general rule that all agree to, so it contradicts רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who allows becoming טמא for a dead father's limb. רב holds like those who require the whole body.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: what 'not for limbs' leaves out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא of רב כהנא בר' אליעזר בן יעקב. It reads 'not for limbs' as leaving out small amounts of a body: a כזית of flesh, a כזית of fluid, and a spoonful of decayed matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches in the name of רב כהנא בר' אליעזר בן יעקב: 'For her he becomes טמא, but not for limbs.' This leaves out a כזית of a dead body, a כזית of fluid from a body, and a full spoon of decayed matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a new ברייתא to challenge רב again. This step is the first half of that ברייתא, and the real point comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא comes from a different תנא, רב כהנא בר' אליעזר בן יעקב. It reads 'not for limbs' as leaving out only small pieces of a body. That raises the question of what happens with bigger parts that are still not a whole body.

keyTerms.meaning: an olive-sized piece of a dead body
fluid that comes out of a dead body
a full spoon of decayed matter from a body

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַב כָּהֲנָא בְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: But it was taught, [in the name of] רב כהנא son of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב:
For her he becomes טמא,
but he does not become טמא for limbs.
This leaves out an olive-sized piece of a dead body,
and an olive-sized amount of fluid from a body,
and a full spoon of decayed matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַב כָּהֲנָא בְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer of step 8, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא that is not רבי יהודה's.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that the father's body must be whole.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step sets up the attack. The ברייתא lists only small amounts as left out, and the next step shows that larger partial bodies are included.

steps.title: Spine, skull, or most of the skeleton are included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one might think a כהן cannot become טמא for a spine, a skull, or most of the skeleton. But the extra words 'ואמרת אליהם' add another kind of טומאה that he may become טמא for. That seems to allow less than a whole body, against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he may not become טמא for a spine, a skull, most of the skeleton's structure, or most of its bones. So the תורה writes 'and say to them,' which adds another kind of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by allowing a כהן to become טמא even for a spine, a skull, or most of the skeleton. This is the point of the challenge to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A spine, a skull, or most of the bones is not a whole body. Yet this ברייתא, taught in the name of רב כהנא בר' אליעזר בן יעקב, allows a כהן to become טמא for them. So it seems the 'whole body' rule that רב requires is not needed. The גמרא's answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: most of the skeleton's structure, and most of the number of its bones

steps.whatToRemember: The barley-bone ברייתא was explained as רבי יהודה's view. But now a second ברייתא, from רב כהנא בר' אליעזר בן יעקב, seems to allow טומאה for a partial body, so רב is challenged again.

phrases.english: One might think he may not become טמא
for the spine and for the skull
and for most of its structure and most of its number [of bones]
[So] it is written: "and say to them,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:1. The פסוק already said 'speak,' so this extra 'say' is there to teach something new.

phrases.english: the פסוק added for you another kind of טומאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 9, where the challenge to רב lands.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a כהן becomes טמא for his father only when the body is whole.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא that is not רבי יהודה's allows טומאה for a spine, a skull, or most of the skeleton. These are partial bodies, which seems to go against רב.
